issues.failure_explanation:
The remark claims that replacing the optimal/clipped step-sizes of Algorithm~ef{algo: geometric MG} by the fixed step-size $\lambda=(d+1)^{-1}$ leaves the contraction factor $q$ of Proposition~ef{lemma: MG contraction} unchanged for the resulting linear method (equation~\eqref{eq: linearized MG contracion}), and justifies this only by citing Theorem~ef{theorem: general result}. That theorem, however, takes the contraction of a solver $\SS_\ell$ (equation~\eqref{eq: contraction of operator}) as hypothesis and merely transfers it to a GPCG contraction; it cannot by itself supply the contraction of the modified linear method, so the justification is circular and the claim is proved nowhere. Moreover the fixed step-size is not a special case of the algorithm's rule: since $
u_{\ell'}\ge(d+1)^{-1}$ always (an element belongs to at most $d+1$ vertex patches, so $\|\sum_zho_{\ell',z}\|^2\le(d+1)\sum_z\|ho_{\ell',z}\|^2$), the optimal rule generically uses $
u_{\ell'}\in((d+1)^{-1},d+1]$, strictly larger than $(d+1)^{-1}$, and the per-level error reduction $\lambda(2
u_{\ell'}-\lambda)\|ho_{\ell'}\|^2$ is then strictly smaller, so the factor does not follow from the optimal-step-size analysis and a priori worsens. Equation~\eqref{eq: linearized MG contracion} is the key hypothesis in the positive-definiteness argument and in the condition estimate $(1+q^2)/(1-q^2)$ of Corollary~ef{corollary: symmetric MG optimality}.

failure_location.quote: All results of this section remain valid. In particular, Theorem~\ref{theorem: general result} implies that $\vec{B}_{\ell}^{\MG}$ fulfills assumption~\eqref{eq: preconditioner assumption}, i.e., \label{eq: linearized MG contracion} |(\vec{I}-\vec{B}_{\ell}^{\MG}\vec{A}_{\ell})\vec{x}_{\ell}|_{\vec{A}_{\ell}} \leq q \, |\vec{x}_{\ell}|_{\vec{A}_{\ell}} \quad \text{for all } \vec{x}_{\ell} \in \R^{N_{\ell}^p}, where $q \in (0,1)$ is the contraction factor from Proposition~\ref{lemma: MG contraction}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a contraction bound for the linearized method with fixed step-size $\lambda=(d+1)^{-1}$ by adapting the multigrid contraction analysis of \cite{IMPS24} to constant step-sizes (the per-level reduction $\lambda(2\nu_{\ell'}-\lambda)\\|\rho_{\ell'}\|^2\ge(d+1)^{-2}\|\rho_{\ell'}\|^2$ is directly computable from the source's formulas), obtaining a factor $q'\in(0,1)$ (possibly $q'>q$); Corollary~\ref{corollary: symmetric MG optimality} then follows with $(1+q'^2)/(1-q'^2)$ in place of $(1+q^2)/(1-q^2)$.
issues.overall_effect: Corollary~\ref{corollary: symmetric MG optimality} — the SPD property and the $h$- and $p$-independent condition bound $(1+q^2)/(1-q^2)$ of the symmetric multigrid preconditioner $\vec{B}^{\SMG}_\ell$ — is unsupported as written; consequently the claims that PCG+sMG is a uniformly contractive optimal solver and that the sMG-based AFEM loop achieves optimal complexity are unreliable until the contraction of the linearized method is established.
issues.title: Contraction of the linearized (fixed step-size) multigrid asserted without proof
issues.why_classification: Filling the gap requires one new but contained lemma (contraction of the linearized multigrid with fixed step-size); the advertised guarantee type — an SPD preconditioner with an $h$- and $p$-independent condition-number bound and linear complexity — survives, with at most a worse constant. Hence more than minor, but no new global proof architecture and no loss of the main result.

issues.failure_explanation: The matrix $\vec{B}^{\uparrow}_0$ as defined does not represent the coarse solve of Algorithm~\ref{algo: symmetric MG} step~(iii): that solve is exact (undamped) and has matrix $\vec{I}^+_0\vec{A}_0^{-1}(\vec{I}^+_0)^T$ applied to the pre-smoothed residual, but the definition sets $\vec{D}_0^+\coloneqq\lambda\vec{A}$ — contradicting the earlier convention $\vec{D}_0^+\coloneqq\vec{A}_0$ — and lets the product run down to $i=0$, inserting an extra coarse-level factor that does not belong to the pre-smoothing. Hence the stated identity $\vec{s}^{\uparrow}_0=\vec{B}^{\uparrow}_0\vec{r}_\ell$ is false as written. The identity actually used downstream, \eqref{eq: symmetric multigrid preconditioned matrix}, is correct and derived separately, so the defect is confined to this intermediate formula.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Set $\vec{D}_0^+\coloneqq\vec{A}_0$ (consistent with the earlier convention) and let the product in $\vec{B}^{\uparrow}_0$ run over the pre-smoothing levels $i=\ell,\dots,1$ only, i.e., $\vec{B}^{\uparrow}_0=\vec{I}^+_0\vec{A}_0^{-1}(\vec{I}^+_0)^T\prod_{i=\ell}^{1}(\vec{I}-\lambda\vec{A}_\ell\vec{I}^+_i(\vec{D}^+_i)^{-1}(\vec{I}^+_i)^T)$.
issues.overall_effect: The intermediate matrix definition of the coarse-solve operator in the symmetric multigrid section is incorrect; no downstream formal result is affected because the analysis uses the separately stated, correct identity~\eqref{eq: symmetric multigrid preconditioned matrix} (Lemma~\ref{lemma: symmetric multigrid} and Corollary~\ref{corollary: symmetric MG optimality}).
issues.title: Coarse-solve matrix $\vec{B}^{\uparrow}_0$ inconsistent with the symmetric multigrid algorithm
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and forced by the exact coarse solve in Algorithm~\ref{algo: symmetric MG}; the separately stated identity~\eqref{eq: symmetric multigrid preconditioned matrix} used by all downstream results is correct, so no substantive claim, guarantee, or advertised scope changes.

The two lemma statements are therefore technically ill-posed as written; presumably $\Cqu$ denotes a mesh constant of $\TT_0$, which is already listed as a dependence, so the qualitative content is unaffected.
